units.title: Mitral Valve Components Diagram, Normal Valve Area, Etiology and the Rheumatic Pathology Chain
units.sec: Mitral Valve Components Diagram, Normal Valve Area, Etiology and the Rheumatic Pathology Chain
units.guide:
The p352 diagram numbers 1a/1b annulus (assymmetrical ellipsoidal fibrous ring), 2a/2b leaflets attached to annulus (posterior 3 lobes), 3a/3b commissures present b/w leaflets, 4 chordae attached to papillary muscle, 5a/5b papillary muscles (medial single vessel supply → involved) and 6 adjacent LV myocardium; normal valve surface area is 4–6 cm².
Etiology is RHD with a 2-decade latent period and death in 2–5 years once symptomatic without intervention. Acute rheumatic fever + valvulitis with MR leads after 15–20 years to RHD (40% of patients) with MS+MR (m/c), MS+AR and AR+AS; chronic inflammation → commisural fusion → fish mouth deformity → calcification → immobilized leaflet → ↑ stenosis, predisposing to thrombosis (m/c left atrial appendage).

units.title: AHA Classification, the ARF Carditis Note, Diastolic Cycle Gradient and Mild-to-Moderate MS Chain
units.sec: AHA Classification, the ARF Carditis Note, Diastolic Cycle Gradient and Mild-to-Moderate MS Chain
units.guide:
AHA stages: progressive >1.5 cm², severe (asymptomatic/symptomatic) <1.5 cm², very severe <1.0 cm²; largest valve is tricuspid and ARF carditis gives 65% MR / 35% MR+AR (p353). Diastole runs S2 → IVR (MV opens incompletely) → gradient → ↑↑ LAP → ↑↑ PCWP → rapid filling → reduced filling → atrial systole; normally LAP = LVEDP – PCWP = PAEDP = 8–10 mmHg.
Mild-moderate MS: stress/exercise/pregnancy/fever/AFib → tachycardia → shortened diastole → ↓ filling time → ↑↑↑ LAP → ↑↑↑ PCWP → dyspnea with orthopnea, PND and pulmonary edema; presentation is dyspnea on tachycardia and β-blocker keeps HR down.

units.title: Severe and Very Severe MS: Pulmonary Hypertension Arms, Second-Stenosis Theory and Forward-Flow Signs
units.sec: Severe and Very Severe MS: Pulmonary Hypertension Arms, Second-Stenosis Theory and Forward-Flow Signs
units.guide:
Severe MS: ↑↑↑↑ PCWP → ↑↑ PAEDP → PHTN via back pressure and reflex pulmonary vasoconstriction; presentation branches RVH→failure, TR, loud palpable P2, prominent pulsations, parasternal heave and prominent v wave (p354). The 2nd-stenosis theory: PHTN → pulmonary vasoconstriction → ↓ blood entering LA → patient feels better but is going to severe MS; very severe MS adds LV failure → ↓ cardiac output.
Forward flow: A2 ↔ OS over IVR; LA ↑↑ opens MV earlier so A2–OS shortens ∝ severity; murmur begins at end of IVR and its longer duration ∝ severity; pre-systolic accentuation is atrial contraction at the end of MDM and is absent in AF; loud S1 follows leaflets open at the bottom (↑ velocity of contraction) with delayed closure.

units.title: Backward Pressure Table, LAP Compression Syndromes, Hemoptysis Causes and the Clinical Findings Table
units.sec: Backward Pressure Table, LAP Compression Syndromes, Hemoptysis Causes and the Clinical Findings Table
units.guide:
Backward pressure: PVH dyspnea, PAH with PHTN→RVH/TR, RAP ↑ JVP, IVC RHF features (ascites, edema) (p355). ↑↑ LAP stretches/dilates atria → AF → hypotensive shock and compresses esophagus (dysphagia) and RLN (hoarseness, Ortner's); LA clots embolise.
Hemoptysis causes: pulmonary apoplexy (↑ LAP rupturing thin-walled pulmonary/bronchial veins), winter (chronic) bronchitis → blood-streaked sputum, pulmonary edema → capillary rupture, anticoagulants, pulmonary infarction/hemosiderosis. Findings table: S1 loud, S2 palpable/wide split (failure), S3/S4 absent, rumbling MDM (left lateral, bell, end-expiration, no radiation); pulse normal/AFib, BP normal, JVP prominent 'a' wave, tapping apex displaced laterally.

units.title: Associated Murmurs, the MDM Note, MS-versus-Austin-Flint Table, ECG P Waves and CXR Findings
units.sec: Associated Murmurs, the MDM Note, MS-versus-Austin-Flint Table, ECG P Waves and CXR Findings
units.guide:
Caravallos sign (pansystolic TR) rises with inspiration at the lower left sternal border; Graham Steele murmur (diastolic decrescendo PR) sits at the same border (p356). MDM murmurs: Carey Coombs (acute MR), TS, Austin Flint (AR), MS. MS vs Austin Flint: AF frequent vs sinus rhythm, tapping vs hyperdynamic apex, loud vs soft S1, OS +++ vs absent, S3 absent vs + in AR with failure, PHTN present vs absent.
ECG: P pulmonale = increased P amplitude (II, V1); P mitrale = enhanced second hump (II) and enhanced negative deflection (V1). CXR straightening of left heart border is due to hypoplastic aorta, dilated pulmonary artery, LVH and ↓ cavity site (as printed).

units.title: Echocardiography, Warfarin and NOAC, PMBV with Contraindications and Balloon Valvotomy Figure
units.sec: Echocardiography, Warfarin and NOAC, PMBV with Contraindications and Balloon Valvotomy Figure
units.guide:
TTE stages MS and shows MR and calcification; TEE rules out LA clots; left atrial myxoma mimics MS (p357). Warfarin is indefinite for AF/clots and NOAC has no role in MS/prosthetic valve issue.
PMBV(C) = percutaneous mitral balloon valvotomy (commisurotomy); contraindications are calcific MS (requires valve replacement), thrombus formation and predominant regurgitation, all bracketed to mitral valve replacement; ↓ heart rate with β-blockers is life saving. The A–D figure carries stiffening cannula and guide wire labels, captioned mitral balloon valvotomy.
